People & perspectives study · Maps to E1 (Leading at Scale — founder-to-operator succession, a COO layer inserted between CEO and CTO), E4 (Governance — first Chair/CEO split, board composition as strategy signal), E7 (Exec Presence & Comms — McVey's "record" letters vs Concannon's "channels" letters), E8 (Stakeholder & IR — three CFOs in three years, KPI drift narrated by the CEO), Course 09 (Leadership & Org Behavior — insiders vs exchange-world hires), E3 (M&A — who speaks, and who goes silent, when a company is sold) · Written 2026-10-25 · Part of marketaxess hub; companions marketaxess outside voices, marketaxess mission forces, marketaxess ice deal, marketaxess strategy financials; mirror note tradeweb people

  • Source: _ingest/raw/marketaxess/articles.jsonl (359 items, Jan 2019 – Oct 23 2026): every leadership-change and board release (~20), all 32 earnings-release narratives, the seven CEO Letters to Stockholders and Clients (FY2019–FY2025), the 2021 Investor Day and Dec 2025 Goldman Sachs decks, the ICE deal release (2026-07-30), and the bylined or interview pieces in which staff speak at length (The TRADE, The DESK, Bloomberg, WatersTechnology, Markets Media reprints, 2025–26). Caveats: (1) everything is company-published; reprints were chosen by MarketAxess; (2) no earnings-call transcripts, so no leader is heard under analyst questioning; (3) many Knowledge Center dates are estimates; (4) titles are taken from the dated release, not the current byline; (5) pronouns are used only where a source states them (McVey, Concannon, Sweeney, Fiszel Bieler, Berry, Lee, Quan, Hernandez, Gerosa); everyone else is they.
  • Core claim: For 23 years MarketAxess was Rick McVey's firm and its identity was his idea: Open Trading, the anonymous all-to-all pool he called "essential to the functioning of credit markets" in the COVID quarter. In Jan 2019 he hired Chris Concannon (ex-Bats CEO, Cboe President, Virtu, Nasdaq, Instinet, SEC attorney) as President & COO; Concannon became CEO on Apr 3 2023 and spent the next three years importing equity-market machinery — order books, algos (Pragma), mid-point sessions (Mid-X), closing auctions, ETF RFQ (RFQ-hub). Around him almost every seat turned over: CFO DeLise → Gerosa (2021) → Fiszel Bieler (2024); a new Group COO (Berry, ex-LSEG, 2025) with the CTO (Baker → Chalamani → Quan, 2026) reporting to him, not the CEO; CIO Themelis → Panchal (2022). The chair split for the first time (Hernandez, ex-JPMorgan, Jan 2025), and the board's additions shifted from strategy-builders (2019–21: Altobello, Prager, Gmelich, Gibson, Li) to deal-literate operators (2023–26: Hernandez, Hoornweg, Cifu, Schiciano). Severance for "changes in management structure" appeared in three quarters (2Q25, 4Q25, 1Q26). Seven and a half months after publishing standalone targets, the company agreed to sell to ICE for $167 a share. Founder conviction built the moat; the operator found the moat alone no longer grew US credit revenue.

What the chart says. - One succession, done slowly. Concannon was visibly the heir for four years (President & COO, director, owner of data and corporate development from Jan 2019). McVey's transition line in the FY22 letter frames it as strength, not crisis: "now is the right time for Chris Concannon, a proven leader deeply experienced in" electronic markets. McVey then stayed as Executive Chairman for 21 months. - Everything else turned over under the new CEO. CFO (2024), a new COO layer (2025), CTO (2026), Americas product (2025), and the earlier EMEA leaders (Roupie, Paranandi) are not seen after 2024. Inference: Concannon rebuilt the top team around operators from exchange, data-vendor and big-bank technology backgrounds. - The board as a strategy map. 2019–21 additions map to the growth plan: a buy-side trader who helped seed Open Trading (Prager), a dealer credit head (Gmelich), a diversity-dealer CEO (Gibson), China market structure (Li). 2023–26 additions map to the endgame: a JPMorgan investment-banking chair (Hernandez), a bank markets head (Hoornweg), a market-maker founder (Cifu) and a private-equity adviser (Schiciano). JPMorgan was later MKTX's financial adviser on the ICE sale and ran the Dec 2025 ASR. (Inference; no release links these.) - Severance as a tell. The releases record repositioning charges "principally severance costs related to changes in management structure" in 2Q25 ($4.0M), 4Q25 ($1.1M) and 1Q26 ($1.5M).

2. Profiles

Rick McVey — founder (2000), Chairman & CEO to Apr 2023, Executive Chairman to Dec 2024

Background: 40 years in fixed income by his own count; launched Open Trading in 2013. Talks about: all-to-all liquidity, client savings larger than revenue, automation, volatility as the swing factor. The voice of every earnings release 2019–22 and of four letters. - All-to-all is the moat. "Without the open market — with its large, diverse pool of different types of participants" there would be more risk, not less (FY19 letter, Apr 2020). "We believe Open Trading liquidity was essential to the functioning of credit markets during the quarter" (1Q20, Apr 29 2020). FY20: "a pivotal year in which Open Trading established itself as an essential source of liquidity" (Apr 2021). - Savings as proof. Clients "saved an estimated total of $1.1 billion in transaction costs, which significantly exceeds the Company’s total revenue in 2020" (FY20 letter). The number halved to $570M in FY21, and he wrote it as resilience: "Despite historically low volatility and tight bid/ask spreads" (FY21 letter). - Automation as the second engine. "The trend to automated execution is gaining momentum in fixed income globally" (Apr 2019). "Trading automation and lower transaction costs on MarketAxess are driving a sustainable change in trading behavior among institutional market participants" (Oct 2020). - Candour about volatility. 2Q21 results were "heavily impacted by low levels of credit market volatility in a very tough year over year comparison for MarketAxess" (Jul 2021). FY22 he admits the Fed cycle "negatively impacted our U.S. high-grade average variable fee per million and dampened our top-line growth." - Public-purpose register. On the NY Fed SMCCF: "MarketAxess is honored to participate in this important program to support the recovery of the American economy" (Sep 2020). Purpose: "to open global markets, creating more opportunities for the companies, institutions, and individuals who depend on them" (FY21 letter). - How his view changed. 2019 automation optimist → 2020 crisis-liquidity evangelist → 2021 defensive (volatility, "broader foundation") → 2022 macro optimist ("creates a long runway for growth in fixed income e-trading", Oct 2022). Exit: "it was an honor to lead this organization from a startup to a position of global leadership" (Nov 2024).

Chris Concannon — President & COO Jan 2019 – Apr 2023, CEO Apr 2023 –

Background: CEO of Bats (led its 2016 IPO and sale to Cboe), then Cboe President & COO; earlier Nasdaq, Virtu, Instinet, and attorney at Morgan, Lewis & Bockius and the SEC (2019 release). Talks about: digitizing credit, ETFs and indexation, data as product, automation and AI, and from 2024 market share, channels and stockholder value. - The import mandate. On joining: "Having been an active participant in the transformational changes of other asset classes," he would help as MarketAxess "continues to digitize the credit markets and build on its record of innovation and growth" (Jan 7 2019). - ETFs and indices first. "We are still in the early days of the indexation of the fixed income markets" (Sweeney hire, Oct 2021). "MarketAxess has a unique view into the traditionally fragmented and less liquid fixed income market" (MKTX 400 index, Mar 2022). - As CEO-designate: automation and data. Clients need technology "to compete more effectively in markets increasingly shaped by automation, data analytics and the growth in ETFs" (Jan 9 2023). Pragma brings "quantitative, AI-powered technology solutions powered by proprietary data designed to simplify and enhance their workflows" (Aug 2023). - 2024: the phone is the target. X-Pro is for "expanding our share of large-sized trades which are principally done over the phone" (1Q24). FY24 letter: "2024 was primarily a “build” year in our technology" and "We have a clear strategy to return to market share growth in U.S. credit across these three channels". - 2025: open admission. "To address our challenges in U.S. credit, we are focused on growing our targeted block trading solution in the client-initiated channel" (3Q25, Nov 2025). FY25 letter: "We still have work to do". - Auctions as signature bet. "There’s no tradeable true auctions. This is the first." He also concedes, in the reporter's paraphrase, that success depends on adoption, and predicts: "Auctions will ultimately grow into other areas of the fixed-income market, particularly the US Treasury market" (Bloomberg, Nov 5 2025). - Dec 2025 → Jul 2026: from targets to scale. "Our announcements today reflect the Board’s confidence in our long-term strategy and our commitment to driving stockholder value creation" (Dec 9 2025). Then, at the sale: "Together, we will have the scale to invest more deeply in the areas that matter most to our customers" (Jul 30 2026), conceding that ICE brings "additional retail and wealth trading protocols, strong data, connectivity". - Read. He arrived to make bonds trade like equities and built every piece (order book, algos, sessions, auctions, ETF RFQ). None of it reversed the US-credit revenue decline the Dec 2025 deck admitted (−2% CAGR 2020–24); the operator-CEO sold to an exchange operator. (Inference.)

Kat Sweeney — Head of Index & ETF Solutions (2021) → Global Head of Data & ETF Solutions

Background: SSGA Head of Institutional Client Group NA; 18 years at Goldman, building ETF market-making (Oct 2021 release). The ETF/auction/data voice, and the most quotable executive of 2025. - Index conviction. "My career is firmly rooted in the belief that index solutions have benefited all market participants" (Oct 2021). "We’ve seen in our data how index products like ETFs are transforming the bond market" (Mar 2022). - Data to valuation. The S&P deal is meant to "close the gaps between best execution, intraday trading decisions and end-of-day valuation" (Oct 2024). - Auctions, borrowed from equities. "Auctions in derivatives and equity markets have proven to reduce volatility, increase transparency and concentrate liquidity" (Nov 2025). "Within the next couple of years, this could be the dominant protocol in the market" and "we’re now in the beginning of the snowball phase" (The TRADE, Dec 15 2025). The candid caveat: "We have to make sure the auction is a liquid event".

Richard Schiffman — Head of Open Trading → Global Head of Trading Solutions

  • Live Markets is "a natural progression of our anonymous trading protocols" (May 2019). The early warning on order books: "a streaming order book requires commitment from all participants to succeed." (May 2021) — the best explanation in the corpus of why Live Markets volume was never disclosed.
  • On non-banks: "Flow Traders is a true change maker, bringing new and important sources of liquidity to the market" (Dec 2021). On automation: some clients run "our strategies for over 90% of their trading volumes" (Sep 2024).

Christophe Roupie — Head of Europe & Asia → Head of EMEA & APAC (2019–23)

  • Brexit readiness as edge: "we were one of the first movers in establishing an office in the Netherlands." (Feb 2019). RRH: "a firm demonstration of our long-term commitment to building our regulatory reporting infrastructure across Europe." (Dec 2020). "We saw a 74% increase in our trading volume across Asia Pacific in 2020." (Sep 2021). Last seen Oct 2023 on Open Trading for 28 local markets. The EMEA/APAC job then went to an outsider (Berry).

David Krein — Global Head of Research & Data

  • "Axess All first pioneered fixed income market transparency 7 years ago, well before the mandates of MiFID II" (Mar 2022). The data-as-product line predates Concannon's ETF push; Krein co-bylined the 2020 Open Trading/ETF research.

Nichola Hunter — CEO of LiquidityEdge (2019) → Head of Rates (2020–21)

  • "Offering an alternative to incumbent trading protocols, LiquidityEdge continues to record daily highs in excess of $25 billion." (Aug 2019). "Our rates trading solution is differentiated by high-quality pricing through bespoke order books and streaming liquidity across the Treasury curve." (Dec 2020). The implicit incumbents are never named; Treasuries stayed a ~2–3.7% share business (per the releases).

Dan Burke — Global Head of EM (2024–)

  • Credits dealers for Targeted RFQ: they wanted "a more contained environment with more transparency on the number of competing dealers" (TRFQ panel, undated ~2024–25). On EM price improvement: "The average price improvement on those smaller trades is 23 cents above the next best disclosed dealer." MENA: "trades using our all-to-all trading protocol Open Trading made up 47% of total MENA volume" (Dec 2025). Mission line: "Our goal is to deliver solutions that not only drive global capital flows into emerging markets" (Dec 2025).

Riad Chowdhury — Head of APAC (2020–)

  • "I always say there’s no Asia." (The TRADE, Jul 2025). "In 2023, the volume traded of Asia, local currency bonds on our platform increased by 42% over the previous year" (Feb 2024). On India: "We’re delighted to be the first platform to be able to bring this new trading capability to international investors." (Jun 2025).

Maria E. Calderon — Head of Sales, Latin America

  • "Request-for-Market (RFM), Switch Trading and now EM Portfolio Trading have all seen rapid and significant adoption" (Nov 2021). "MarketAxess is in the perfect position to help our clients navigate the nuances of e-trading" (GlobalCapital awards piece, May 2024).

Erik Tham — Head of Product, Global Private Banking

  • The wealth voice before ICE claimed wealth. "There is no ‘Stocks’ app for fixed income markets." (Axess IQ blog, undated). On Asia automation: "It is available, it is mature, and Asia is gradually catching up" (Hubbis, Sep 2022).

Spencer Lee — client (2021), then Head of Client Products, Americas (May 2025–)

The revolving door in one person. In the Sept 2021 Investor Day deck he is quoted as a client — "Spencer Lee, Agilon Capital" — praising automation as "this new frontier of automation will be a critical tool." Four years later he was hired: "I’ve spent most of my career on a pursuit of building the best buy-side trader workflows in the market" (May 2025). - Orchestration over tools. "Automation isn’t just about efficiency anymore, it’s about expanding what’s achievable." "Our goal isn’t more tools, it’s better orchestration of them." He wants a "smart protocol chooser" and admits more protocols means "this also multiplies the number of decisions needed" (The DESK, Jun 15 2026). On leakage: matching must be "done with great care to guard against information leakage". - Post-deal, he fronts the IMTC integration: "we are embedding that liquidity directly into the investment workflow" (Sep 2026).

Dean Berry — Group COO & CEO EMEA/APAC (2025–)

Background: LSEG Group Head of Workflows and interim co-head of Data & Analytics; earlier BGC; 16 years a fixed-income trader. Hired with "my track record of profitable product-led innovation" (May 2025). The new No. 2, owner of technology, product, risk and international — and an alumnus of Tradeweb's controlling shareholder. - TraX Tape: "Market participants have more data than ever but turning that data into actionable insight remains a challenge" and "The data tells you what happened, and TraX Tape tells you what it means." (Jun 2026). Hiring Quan: to "more deeply embed AI and advanced analytics across our products and workflows" (Feb 2026).

Steve Tait — Head of US Dealer Execution (2025–)

25+ years at JPMorgan, last overseeing systematic market making. Mid-X gives "better tools for dealers to recycle risk generated by increased portfolio trading" (Aug 2025). Forecast: "there could potentially be a world with continuous mid-point matching." (Markets Media, Dec 2025). The dealer-initiated channel is the one Concannon calls the strategic focus, per the interviewer.

Gareth Coltman, Julien Alexandre, Daniel Kelly, Paulo Costa — the product and research bench

  • Coltman (automation): "Adaptive Auto-X is an exciting leap forward in intelligent automation" (Jun 2023).
  • Alexandre (research): CP+ is "crucial in munis where trading is known to be sporadic" (Dec 2024); "Our AI models excel at extracting pricing signals from multiple data sources".
  • Kelly (munis): "The portfolio trading tool was among the most requested enhancements to our Municipal bond franchise." (Jun 2024).
  • Costa (data, EMEA/APAC): the wittiest line in the corpus — "our clients have an absolute craving for transparency but potentially not their own." (Jul 2025). He sells a give-to-get model because Asia has no TRACE.

The CFOs — DeLise, Gerosa, Fiszel Bieler

The finance chair is nearly mute in this corpus, as Tradeweb's was (tradeweb people). - DeLise (to Aug 2021) is praised by McVey for helping "steer our firm through the early days of electronic trading adoption" and moved to IR/Corp Dev. - Gerosa (Aug 2021 – Jan 2024) speaks once, leaving: the team "established new product cylinders to drive future growth" (Nov 2023). The 1Q22 release-format reset (EBITDA first) came on his watch. (Inference.) - Fiszel Bieler (May 2024 –), ex-State Street IR head: joining "at a time when industry demand for technology and efficiency has never been higher" (Feb 2024). Concannon: she "has brought additional insight and rigor to our finance operations" (FY24 letter). She co-presented the Dec 2025 targets; there is no quote from her on them or on the sale.

The board voices — Casper, Altobello, Hernandez, Hoornweg, Cifu, Schiciano, the 2019–21 class

  • Casper (Lead Independent, Jan 2023): "we are fortunate to have in Chris a proven leader deeply experienced in electronic markets."
  • Altobello (2023): "This company has a strong record of accomplishment and, I believe, an even greater opportunity ahead."
  • Hernandez: rejoining, "MarketAxess is at the forefront of important market structure and technology innovations" (Sep 2023); as Chair-elect, "as we find new ways to make one of the world’s leading fixed income marketplaces even better" (Nov 2024). Chaired the Compensation and Talent Committee before the chair.
  • Hoornweg (Jan 2025): "a time where the appetite for technology and efficiency has never been higher" — almost the same sentence as Fiszel Bieler's, a house template.
  • Cifu appears twice, seven years apart. As Virtu CEO and partner (Apr 2019): "Clients of MarketAxess will have access to Virtu’s leading ETF platform RFQ-hub". As director (Jan 2026): "a company that sits at the forefront of the digital transformation in fixed‑income trading". Schiciano: "market structure, data, and technology are increasingly central to liquidity and transparency".
  • 2019–21 class: Prager: "MarketAxess has been an important catalyst in the accelerating transformation of global fixed income markets" (Jul 2019). Gmelich: "Technology is at the heart of innovation in financial markets today and MarketAxess is helping shape the future" (Oct 2019). Gibson: "MarketAxess stands out as one of the most successful growth companies in financial technology" (Jul 2020).
  • Missing: any board voice on the Dec 2025 strategic review, the ASR, or the ICE sale. The deal release says only that it was "unanimously approved by the Boards of Directors of both companies".

ICE on the deal — Jeff Sprecher and Warren Gardiner

  • Sprecher (ICE Chair & CEO) places MarketAxess in a pattern: "take the largest, least-efficient corners of global finance and apply technology and network effects to improve transparency". "That is what we did in energy, in credit default swaps, and in mortgage technology." "Acquiring MarketAxess is the natural next step in that journey."
  • Gardiner (ICE CFO): "We are acquiring a high-quality, cash-generative business" and "our balance sheet strength allows us to finance this acquisition entirely in cash".
  • Read: the buyer's language is about efficiency and cash; the seller's is about scale and complementarity. Nobody on either side mentions Open Trading. See marketaxess ice deal and ice hub.

Issue Earlier view (who, when) Later / contrasting view (who, when) Read
What the moat is McVey: Open Trading "essential" (2020); "reflecting the powerful benefits of Open Trading, our unique all-to-all liquidity pool" (Jan 2023) Concannon: the "MarketAxess advantage" of network, "differentiated liquidity" and AI data (FY25 letter); Berry: what TraX Tape "means" (2026) All-to-all is demoted from identity to one plank. The moat migrates from who you can reach to what you know

Volatility McVey: low volatility "heavily impacted" results (2021); "The macro backdrop is now much improved" (2Q22) Concannon: "continued tight credit spreads and low credit spread volatility" (FY25 letter) Both CEOs blame calm markets; neither sold a protocol that earns in calm. The founder said it more bluntly
Market share talk McVey FY20: HG 21.6%, HY 14.6%, records everywhere FY23 letter: no share figures; FY24: "return to market share growth"; FY25: "drive U.S. credit revenue growth" Share language disappears as share falls (HG 18.4% in 4Q24 vs 20.9%) — see marketaxess strategy financials
The phone McVey 2019–21: automation "fueling a new round of growth" Concannon: blocks "principally done over the phone" (2024); Bailey recreates IDB "white-glove service" (2025); Tait: dealers "on the phone with that broker" The operator admits the hard tail is human; the product answer becomes high-touch-plus-electronic
Dealers McVey: dealers "tapping Open Trading to source liquidity" (FY19) Concannon: auctions let dealers "exit inventory" or provide liquidity (2025); Tait's dealer suite; Bloomberg's framing that auctions may squeeze dealer profits From dealers-as-participants-in-all-to-all to dealers-as-a-customer-channel
Standalone vs sale Concannon: "the Board’s confidence in our long-term strategy" (Dec 2025); "confident in the strategy we have put in place" (FY25 letter, Apr 29 2026) Concannon: "we will have the scale" (Jul 30 2026) Thirteen weeks between the letter and the sale. Merger costs were already booked in 1Q26 as "other legal expenses" (reclassified later)
AI Composite+ is "AI-based" (FY19) and "A.I.-powered" (FY21) "accelerating our use of artificial intelligence" (FY25); Quan to embed AI; Lee: orchestration MKTX had ML pricing early; the rhetoric arrived late, like Tradeweb's

The three sharpest shifts: (1) Moat, 2020 → 2025: all-to-all breadth → proprietary data plus curated routing. (2) Scoreboard, 2020 → 2025: HG share → composite → channels → "revenue growth". (3) Ownership, Dec 2025 → Jul 2026: standalone targets and a debt-funded ASR → "scale" through a sale.

4. Communication style and narrative craft

McVey — the founder-salesman. Short, declarative, numbers-forward letters: "11th straight", "12th consecutive", "13th consecutive" year of records; savings set against revenue; a TAM framed as big-bank FICC revenue ($84B) against e-trading revenue (~$2B). He reaches for civic language in crises ("recovery of the American economy") and always closes by thanking employees. He rarely forecasts beyond "long runway".

Concannon — the exchange operator. He speaks in microstructure: order-centric, multi-protocol, channels, sessions, auctions, orchestration. He organises the business into frameworks that change (three channels from 2024; "MarketAxess advantage" from 2025) and admits problems in operator's terms — build year, "challenges in U.S. credit", "We still have work to do" — never with a number for share lost. His best lines are in interviews, not letters ("This is the first.").

The bench — metaphor-light, data-heavy. Sweeney's "snowball phase" and "bands of arbitrage"; Costa's "craving for transparency"; Chowdhury's "there’s no Asia"; Berry's "what it means". The research arm (Alexandre, quant analysts) argues by chart; it is the most self-critical voice in the firm (see marketaxess open trading).

Recurring house phrases (first sightings): preferred all-to-all trading solution (boilerplate from Apr 2019); Open Trading is how (What's New ads); intelligent (FY24 mission onward); differentiated liquidity (2025); three channels (2024); white-glove service (DealerAxess, 2025); record (every release).

What they never talk about: - Competitors by name. No leader names Tradeweb, Bloomberg or Trumid as a rival; Tradeweb and Bloomberg appear only as consolidated-tape JV partners (2022–23). Tradeweb's newsroom returns the favour (tradeweb outside voices §6). - Fees. Credit fee per million fell from $184.78 (FY21) to $127 (3Q26), per the releases; no leader discusses pricing to clients beyond "mix". - Why executives left. Gerosa's departure gets the courtesy quote; Roupie, Paranandi, Panchal and Chalamani simply stop appearing. - The sale process. No board member explains the strategic review or why a sale beat the targets. - Headcount and culture after the ESG era. Headcount is a table number (858 at 3Q26); the culture section disappears with ESG after FY23.

5. Culture and talent, as the leaders describe it

  • Founder culture: clients plus collaboration. McVey's FY19 letter: "we prize collaboration with our clients and with our colleagues". DeLise praised for "our principles of transparency and collaboration" (2021).
  • COVID remote access as a service story. Over 10,000 remote users were set up in March 2020; the FY20 letter thanks employees "for their dedication to our clients and to each other in a stressful time."
  • DEI and ESG, then silence. The Diversity Dealer Initiative (May 2021; pilot with Loop, Seelaus, BlackRock and AB; board link via Gibson), Trading for Trees, ESG reports with "long-term diversity and human capital goals" tied to management pay (FY21 letter). ESG has a section in FY23 and vanishes in FY24–25. (The drop is a fact; the reason is not stated.)
  • Talent imports by function. Exchange/market-structure (Concannon), ETF market-making (Sweeney), bank technology (Panchal, Quan), data vendor (Berry), buy-side quant trader (Lee), bank dealer algos (Tait), bank markets (Hoornweg on the board). Internal promotions are mostly in finance (Gerosa) and product (Coltman, Schiffman).
  • What is absent. Any employee survey or workplace award; attrition; equity culture after a share price that rose 411% in five years (FY20 letter) and then fell; integration of Pragma, MuniBrokers and RFQ-hub teams; what happens to staff under ICE's $100M synergy target.

6. Leadership lenses

  • canon kotter leading change — the founder-to-operator handover was a model guided coalition: four years as President, an announced date, the founder as Executive Chairman. The change that followed (protocol rebuild) lacked the second half of Kotter: short-term wins visible in the KPI the market watched (US credit share).
  • canon christensen innovators dilemma — McVey's all-to-all was a disruptive entry against dealer RFQ in 2013. By 2024 MKTX was the incumbent defending RFQ revenue while Tradeweb won by wiring the workflow around the trade (tradeweb credit).
  • canon pfeffer power — who holds power shows in reporting lines: CTO reports to a COO from LSEG; the Chair is a JPMorgan banker; a market-maker founder joins the board six months before a sale. Power moved from founder to board and buyer.
  • canon schein organizational culture — artifact: the preferred all-to-all boilerplate, unchanged since 2019. Espoused value: open markets. Basic assumption (founder era): anonymity and breadth beat relationships. Concannon's protocols quietly reversed that assumption (targeted, disclosed, curated) while the artifact stayed.
  • canon grove high output management — indicators: the firm swapped its indicators (share → composite → channels) while performance worsened. Grove would call that losing the paired indicator.
  • canon bezos shareholder letters — McVey's letters repeat a metric streak; Concannon's rebuild the framework each year and never restate the last year's forecast (FY24's "benefits in the second half of 2025").
  • canon jensen meckling agency theory — a debt-funded $300M ASR (Dec 2025) followed by a cash sale at a 33% premium. Ask whose time horizon each decision served.

Part A (E4, governance): You are the Lead Independent Director in Dec 2025. Using only facts in this note, write the three questions you would ask before approving the $300M ASR funded with $220M of revolver debt. Worked answer: (1) US credit revenue shrank at a 2% CAGR 2020–24 and HG share fell from 20.9% to 18.4% in a year — what share recovery do the 8–9% revenue targets assume, and by when? (2) We have changed CFO three times since 2021 and inserted a COO above the CTO; is the management team that will deliver 2026–28 in place? (3) Is any strategic alternative under discussion that would make buying back stock at today's price a transfer to sellers? (Seven months later the board approved a sale at a 33% premium.)

Part B (E7): Rewrite Concannon's FY25 sentence "We still have work to do" as McVey would have written it. Model: McVey would lead with a record and a dollar figure — e.g., record $846M revenue (17th consecutive), $5.3T of inquiries, 440M+ responses — then name the work as an investment, not a gap. Then ask: which version tells an investor more? (Concannon's, because it admits the gap; McVey's style is what let share loss stay invisible in 2021–23.)

Part C (Course 09): Predict each person's answer to Should a $10M illiquid HY block go to Open Trading by default? — McVey 2020 (yes: all-to-all is essential), Schiffman 2021 (only if all sides commit), Burke 2025 (no: targeted RFQ, contained dealer set), Lee 2026 (let the smart protocol chooser decide, guard against leakage), Sweeney 2025 (put it in the closing auction if it is an index name). Score yourself on house phrases.
